title: Using in-line signals to predict viable-cell yield across iPSC-derived production lots
summary: Across 16 simulated iPSC-derived production lots (same donor material, medium, and feed), viable-cell yield still swung from about 1.35 to 4.68 ×10⁹ cells per lot. Invert Assist read all 16 lots as one dataset, built an in-line soft sensor that predicts harvest viable-cell count to within about 5–10% from reactor signals alone, and traced the swing to a single controllable variable: differentiation-trigger timing. A lot switched 48 hours late overshot in expansion, then crashed, and the soft sensor flagged it about 60 hours before the release assay could. (Simulated demonstration data.)
